analysis.title: GS Crook - GS MORNING: 1) Connecting you to GS, 2) Data Centre Forecasts, 3) NZD Update, 4) Latest FX Trader and 5) Week Ahead Previews (9 Nov 2026)
key_insights: The Adam Crook morning note is a link digest covering five items: Connecting you to GS, Data Centre Forecasts, NZD Update, Latest FX Trader and Week Ahead Previews. Only the first item's content is in the extracted text. The other four are headline references only.

The note poses key questions from the GS floor: takeaways from the US midterms, implications for macro (FX, rates, EM), El Nino and when winter forecasts become relevant for TTF and Aggs, whether equities after the midterms are a buying opportunity or face structural headwinds, and what US payrolls say about the labour market and the AI labor force and productivity debate. The extracted text does not give GS's answers to these.

Alec Phillips (Chief US Political Economist) says the biggest surprise for data centres and AI on election night was at the state level, not the federal level. It centred on Texas, where he says there was roughly a 65% chance going in that Governor Abbott would win re-election.
At the federal level, Phillips expects some focus on data centres but nothing too extreme. He names ratepayer protections and possibly removing some existing tax incentives.

At the state level, Phillips says the issue is moratoria on permitting. With gubernatorial wins in Texas, Georgia and Ohio, he says up to around 40% of planned data centre capacity is in theory affected.
Phillips thinks a temporary moratorium lasting several months, until new rules are in place, is a possible outcome.
risk_factors: State-level permitting moratoria on data centres after the midterms, with up to around 40% of planned capacity in theory affected (per Alec Phillips).
Federal measures aimed at data centres, including ratepayer protections and possible removal of some existing tax incentives (per Alec Phillips).
